problems.title: Distance between quadratic roots
problems.question: Find the difference between the roots of 4x²−16x+15=0.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The roots are 3/2 and 5/2. The larger minus smaller is 1.

problems.title: Square an equality of nonnegative quantities
problems.question: Find the root sum of √(x²−4x+7)=5.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: Its discriminant is positive, and every root makes the radicand25, so both are valid. Their sum is 4 by Vieta.

problems.title: Simplify a radical fraction before substituting
problems.question: Evaluate(√a/√b+√b/√a−2)÷[(√a−√b)/(√(ab)(√a+√b))], for a=9, b=6.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: Multiplying by the reciprocal cancels one factor√a−√b and √(ab), leaving(√a−√b)(√a+√b)=a−b.
Thus the value is 9−6=3.

problems.title: External common tangent length
problems.question: Circles have radii1,7 and centre distance 10. Find the segment length of their external common tangent.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The right triangle formed by the radii and tangent has L=√(100−36)=8.

problems.title: Internal common tangent length
problems.question: Circles have radii3,5 and centre distance 10. Find their internal common tangent segment.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The perpendicular radius separation is 3+5=8, so L=√(100−64)=6.

problems.title: Two intersections need a positive discriminant
problems.question: Which listeda makes y=x² and y=ax−7 intersect twice?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: Require|a|>√28≈5.292. Among−3,−1,0,4,5,6, only 6 qualifies.

problems.title: The two radical domains do not meet
problems.question: Solve√(10−2x)·√(x−8)=0.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: The first root requiresx≤5, the secondx≥8.
steps: No real input satisfies both, so the product is never real-defined and has no root.

problems.title: Add two binary integers
problems.question: a=10101₂, b=1110₂. Finda+b in decimal.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.

problems.title: The shortest altitude meets the longest side
problems.question: A triangle has sides 7,9,12. Find its smallest altitude.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: Heron’s formula gives S=√[s(s−7)(s−9)(s−12)], with s=14.
steps: ThusS=√(14·7·5·2)=14√5. Sinceh=2S/base, the smallest altitude uses the largest base12.
Its length is 28√5/12=7√5/3.

problems.title: A line through an intersection parallel to the centres
problems.question: Two radius-R circles have centres distance R apart. Through an intersection C, draw the line parallel to the centre line, meeting the circles again at A, B. FindAB.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: Use centres(0,0),(R,0). Their upper intersection is C=(R/2,√3R/2).
steps: On the horizontal line through C, the first circle’s other point is A=(−R/2,√3R/2); the second’s is B=(3R/2,√3R/2).
ThusAB=3R/2−(−R/2)=2R.

problems.title: Order three close radical values
problems.question: Ordera=3+√2, b=2+√5, c=2√5 increasingly.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The values are b≈4.236, a≈4.414, c≈4.472. Thusb<a<c.

problems.title: Rationalise two unit-denominator conjugates
problems.question: Evaluate(√20+√28)[1/(√7−√6)−1/(√6−√5)].
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: Their difference is √7−√5. The first factor is 2(√5+√7).
The product is 2(7−5)=4.

problems.title: Use the radical domain to remove an absolute value
problems.question: Simplify(x²−9)/√(x²−6x+9)+(√(2−x))².
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The fraction is(x−3)(x+3)/(3−x)=−x−3. The last term is 2−x.
Their sum is −1−2x, onx≤2.

problems.title: Diagonals of a rhombus
problems.question: A rhombus has perimeter68 and diagonal sum 46. Find the absolute diagonal difference.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: The side is 17; half-diagonals are perpendicular, so d₁²+d₂²=4·17²=1156.
steps: Using(d₁−d₂)²=2(d₁²+d₂²)−(d₁+d₂)² gives 2312−2116=196.
The positive difference is 14.

problems.title: Add squared legs instead of simplifying each leg
problems.question: A right triangle has legs(3−√7)/(√2+√6) and √[(3√7+8+8√3)/(4+2√3)]. Find its hypotenuse median.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: The first squared leg is(8−3√7)/(4+2√3). The second squared leg is the given fraction.
steps: Adding cancels√7 and gives(16+8√3)/(4+2√3)=4.
Thus the hypotenuse is 2. Its median from the right vertex has half that length,1.

problems.title: Three radical inequalities on their actual domains
problems.question: Which of the three printed inequalities A, B, C holds for every input in its domain?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: A uses t+1/t≥2 for t>0; B follows by squaring; C’s right side simplifies to(x²−25)/x.
steps: ForB, x≥5. Squaring reduces it to √(x²−25)≤x, which is true.
ForC, x>5 orx<−5. Ifx<−5, the right side is negative while the radical is positive. Ifx>5, writeu=√(x²−25)<x; then the right sideu²/x<u.
All three inequalities hold on their respective domains.

problems.title: Evaluate a cubic at three
problems.question: Which listed coefficient quadruple(a, b, c, d) gives P(3)=47 for P(x)=ax³+bx²+cx+d?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: For(1,2,0,2), the value is 27+18+0+2=47. The other listed quadruples give40,55,51,44,41.

problems.title: Maximise a square root via its radicand
problems.question: f(x)=√(7−x²+6x) has maximum b at x=a. Finda+b.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The radicand is largest16 at x=3. Thusa=3, b=4, and their sum is 7.

problems.title: Orthogonal cyclic diagonals fix a perpendicular direction
problems.question: A cyclic quadrilateral has perpendicular diagonals meeting at M. The line through M perpendicular to AB meets CD at N. IfMD=6, MC=8, find MN.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: PutM=(0,0), A=(a,0), C=(−8,0), B=(0, b), D=(0,−6). Intersecting chords give8a=6b, so b/a=4/3.
steps: AB has slope−b/a=−4/3, so MN has direction(4,3). WriteN=(−4t,−3t).
LineCD has equationx/8+y/6=−1. Substitution givest=1.
ThusMN=√(4²+3²)=5.

problems.title: Compass-and-straightedge constructions
problems.question: Which are constructible:tangents from an exterior point; external common tangents of unequal disjoint circles; a triangle from its three medians?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: Tangency uses a circle on a diameter; common tangents use a difference-radius auxiliary circle; centroid distances are two thirds of medians.
steps: A:join the exterior point to the centre and draw the circle on that segment as diameter. Its intersections locate the tangent contacts.
B:draw the auxiliary circle with radius equal to the radius difference about the larger centre. Tangents from the other centre give the required directions.

C:writep=2m₁/3, q=2m₂/3, r=2m₃/3. ConstructtriangleGUV of sides GU=p, GV=q, UV=r. ReflectV through G to get B, take A=U, and construct C byvector GC=GV−GU. ThenGA+GB+GC=0 and the three centroid distances are p, q, r.
problems.answer: All three, when the median lengths describe a nondegenerate triangle.
problems.note: Three arbitrary lengths need not be valid medians. The construction question is interpreted with the usual feasibility condition.

problems.title: A radical zero adds a root
problems.question: Find the root sum of(2x²−9x+9)√(x−2)=0.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: Its roots are 3/2 and 3, but only 3 is in the domain. The radical also vanishes at x=2.
The distinct roots 2,3 sum to 5.

problems.title: Exactly one valid rational-equation root
problems.question: Find the sum of alla for which(x²−6x+a)/(x²−4)=0 has exactly one real root.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: Exclude x=±2. A repeated numerator root occurs at a=9; an excluded root occurs at a=8 or −16.
steps: For a=9, the double root 3 is valid. For a=8, the numerator roots 2,4 leaveonly4. For a=−16, the roots −2,8 leaveonly8.
Every other real parameter gives either zero roots or two valid distinct roots.
The requested parameter sum is 9+8−16=1.

problems.title: Square numbers with two binary ones
problems.question: A three-digit decimal square has exactly two1s in binary. Which listed digit sum can it have?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: Such a number is 2^i+2^j, with i>j≥0. Check squares n² for 10≤n≤31.
steps: The qualifying squares are 144=128+16=12² and 576=512+64=24². Their decimal digit sums are 9 and 18.
Only 9 is listed.

problems.title: A right angle inside a rectangle
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, F is midpoint CD, K∈BF, BK=8, KF=2, and AKD=90°. FindAB·BC.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
steps: The right angle gives AK·DK=0, or −4w²/25+9h²/25=0. Thus4w²=9h².
BF=10 givesw²+h²/4=100. Henceh²=40, w²=90.
The requested are a is wh=√(40·90)=60.

problems.title: Distance between an incenter and an excenter
problems.question: A right triangle has B=30° and inradius10. Its opposite-B excircle touches leg AC externally and the extensions of BA, BC. Find the distance between circle centres.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity and retain the original domain.
formulas: In a 30°–60°–90° triangle, the opposite-B exradius is √3 times the inradius. Both centres lie on the internal B-bisector at distancesradius/sin15° from B.
steps: For short legb, the semiperimeter is(3+√3)b/2 and s−b=(1+√3)b/2. Thusr_B/r=s/(s−b)=√3.
The centre separation is(10√3−10)/sin15°. Using sin15°=(√6−√2)/4, it simplifies to 20√2.
